【History】 ● To document and classify epileptiform discharges in patients with recurrent seizures and epilepsy. 【Technical description】 ● A 21-channel digital EEG recording with single-channel electrocardiogram and electrodes are placed according to 10-20 International System of Electrode Placement. ● Bandpass filters of 3 to 70 Hz and sensitivity of 200 uVp-p. Notch filter 60 Hz. ● Modality: Resting state EEG. 【EEG description】 ● Background: (1) Posterior dominant rhythm in the most alert state 7-8 Hz, 50uV; normal reactivity to external stimuli. (2) Level of alertness clear (3) Sleep: not fall asleep ● Epileptiform and Nonepileptiform features: (1) Epileptiform features: nil. (2) Electroclinical seizure: nil. (3) Nonepileptiform features: mo; (4) Artifacts: continuous muscle activity, >50% of the tracing involving right temporal electrodes (5) Single-channel electrocardiogram: Normal. ● Intermittent photic stimulation no augmentation of slowing ● Hyperventilation omitted. 【Impression】 Minimally abnormal. ● Minimally slowing of the background activity 【Clinical correlation】 ● Diffuse slowing of the background activity reflects a minimally diffuse cortical dysfunction, which can be seen with toxic-metabolic or systemic causes, or neurodegenerative disorders, and also with cortical injury. 【History】 - To document and classify epileptiform discharges and nonepileptiform features in the patient with recurrent seizures and epilepsy. 【Technical description】 - A 21-channel digital EEG recording with single-channel electrocardiogram and electrodes are placed according to 10-20 International System of Electrode Placement. - Bandpass filters of 3 to 70 Hz and sensitivity of 200 uVp-p. Notch filter 60 Hz. - Modality: Resting state EEG. 【EEG description】 ● Background: - Posterior dominant rhythm in the most alert state: 8-10Hz, 80 uV; normal reactivity to external stimuli. - Level of alertness: clear. - Sleep: stage N2 with alpha dropout, vertex sharp waves, K complex, spindles - Specific characteristics: voltage augmentation ● Epileptiform and Nonepileptiform features: - Epileptiform features: Intermittent single spike and wave in right frontal regions (e.g., 09:08:20), with secondary bilateral synchrony (e.g, 09:17:05) or polyspike (e.g, 09:15:09) - Electroclinical seizure: nil. - Nonepileptiform features: Rare short-run polymorphic theta to delta waves in left frontoparietotemporal regions and bifrontal regions. - Artifacts: eye movements or muscle activity, <50% of the tracing involving <50% of the electrodes - Single-channel electrocardiogram: Normal ● Intermittent photic stimulation: no augmentation of slowing. ● Hyperventilation: omitted. 【Impression】 Abnormal. - Right frontal spike-and-wave - Left frontoparietotemporal and bifrontal slowing 【Clinical correlation】 - Focal slowing suggests an underlying lesion involving the white matter of the ipsilateral hemisphere. - The right frontal spike-and-wave suggest focal hypersynchrony in a patient with a clinical diagnosis of epilepsy. Reference: Tatum IV, W. O., Selioutski, O., Ochoa, J. G., Clary, H. M., Cheek, J., Drislane, F. W., & Tsuchida, T. N. (2016). American clinical neurophysiology society guideline 7: guidelines for EEG reporting. The Neurodiagnostic Journal, 56(4), 285-293.

【History】 - To document and classify epileptiform discharges and nonepileptiform features in the patient with recurrent seizures and epilepsy. 【Technical description】 - A 21-channel digital EEG recording with single-channel electrocardiogram and electrodes are placed according to 10-20 international system of electrode placement. - Bandpass filters of 3 to 70 Hz and sensitivity of 200 uVp-p. Notch filter 60 Hz. - Modality: Resting state EEG. 【EEG description】 ● Background: - Posterior dominant rhythm in the most alert state: 7-8 Hz, 60-70 uV; normal reactivity to external stimuli. - Level of alertness: clear. - Sleep: not fall asleep. ● Epileptiform and Nonepileptiform features: - Epileptiform features: nil. - Electroclinical seizure: nil. - Nonepileptiform features: cc- Artifacts: eye movements or muscle activity, <50% of the tracing involving <50% of the electrodes - Single-channel electrocardiogram: Normal. ● Intermittent photic stimulation: no augmentation of slowing. ● Hyperventilation: no augmentation of slowing. 【Impression】 Abnormal. - Frequent run of generalized high voltage regular or irregular theta waves - Mild slowing of the background activity 【Clinical correlation】 - Diffuse slowing of the background activity reflects a mild diffuse cortical dysfunction, which can be seen with toxic-metabolic or systemic causes, or neurodegenerative disorders, and also with cortical injury. Reference: Tatum IV, W. O., Selioutski, O., Ochoa, J. G., Clary, H. M., Cheek, J., Drislane, F. W., & Tsuchida, T. N. (2016). American clinical neurophysiology society guideline 7: guidelines for EEG reporting. The Neurodiagnostic Journal, 56(4), 285-293. Quantitation of description above: - Prevalence of epileptiform discharges: rare (<1/1hr); occasional (1/1hr-1/1min); frequent (1/1min-1/10s); abundant (>1/10s, not periodic) - Prevalence: continuous (90% of record/epoch); abundant (50-89%); frequent (10-49%); occasional (1-9%); rare (<1%) - Duration of pattern: very long (>60min); long (5min-59min); intermediate duration (1min-4.9min); brief (10-59s); very brief (<10s)

Notch filter 60 Hz. - Modality: Resting state EEG. 【EEG description】 ● Background: - Posterior dominant rhythm in the most alert state: 12 Hz, 60-70 uV; normal reactivity to external stimuli. - Level of alertness: clear. - Sleep: stage N2 with alpha dropout, vertex sharp waves, K complex, spindles Some bilateral asymmetry vertex sharp waves (e.g, 13:24:13; 13:21:39) Frequent vertex sharp waves followed by spindles (vertex-spindles complex). ● Epileptiform and Nonepileptiform features: - Epileptiform features: nil. - Electroclinical seizure: nil. - Nonepileptiform features: nil. - Artifacts: eye movements or muscle activity, <50% of the tracing involving <50% of the electrodes - Single-channel electrocardiogram: Normal. Arrhythmia. ● Intermittent photic stimulation: no augmentation of slowing. ● Hyperventilation: omitted. 【Impression】 Normal. 【Clinical correlation】 nil. Reference: Tatum IV, W. O., Selioutski, O., Ochoa, J. G., Clary, H. M., Cheek, J., Drislane, F. W., & Tsuchida, T. N. (2016). American clinical neurophysiology society guideline 7: guidelines for EEG reporting. 【History】 - To document and classify epileptiform discharges and nonepileptiform features in the patient with recurrent seizures and epilepsy. 【Technical description】 - A 21-channel digital EEG recording with single-channel electrocardiogram and electrodes are placed according to 10-20 International System of Electrode Placement. - Bandpass filters of 3 to 70 Hz and sensitivity of 200 uVp-p. Notch filter 60 Hz. - Modality: Resting state EEG. 【EEG description】 ● Background: - Posterior dominant rhythm in the most alert state: 8-9 Hz, 70-80 uV; normal reactivity to external stimuli. - Level of alertness: clear. - Sleep: stage N2 with alpha dropout, vertex sharp waves, K complex, spindles ● Epileptiform and Nonepileptiform features: - Epileptiform features: nil. - Electroclinical seizure: nil. - Nonepileptiform features: Intermittent polymorphic delta activities over bilateral temporal regions, bilateral asynchronous, single or couplet or in a train. - Artifacts: eye movements or muscle activity, <50% of the tracing involving <50% of the electrodes - Single-channel electrocardiogram: Normal. ● Intermittent photic stimulation: no augmentation of slowing. ● Hyperventilation: omitted. 【Impression】 Abnormal. - Bilateral temporal delta slowing - Mild slowing of the background activity 【Clinical correlation】 - Focal slowing may suggest an underlying lesion involving the white matter of the ipsilateral hemisphere. - Diffuse slowing of the background activity reflects a mild diffuse cortical dysfunction, which can be seen with toxic-metabolic or systemic causes, or neurodegenerative disorders, and also with cortical injury. Reference: Tatum IV, W. O., Selioutski, O., Ochoa, J. G., Clary, H. M., Cheek, J., Drislane, F. W., & Tsuchida, T. N. (2016). American clinical neurophysiology society guideline 7: guidelines for EEG reporting. The Neurodiagnostic Journal, 56(4), 285-293.

【History】 - To document and classify epileptiform discharges and nonepileptiform features in the patient with recurrent seizures and epilepsy. 【Technical description】 - A 21-channel digital EEG recording with single-channel electrocardiogram and electrodes are placed according to 10-20 International System of Electrode Placement. - Bandpass filters of 3 to 70 Hz and sensitivity of 200 uVp-p. Notch filter 60 Hz. - Modality: Resting state EEG. 【EEG description】 ● Background: - Dominant background activity: 6-8 Hz, 50 uV, poor reactivity to external stimuli. - Level of alertness: clear. - Sleep: not asleep. ● Epileptiform and Nonepileptiform features: - Epileptiform features: Frequent asynchronous delta waves in bilateral frontal regions, with intermittent sharpish waves, emphasis on right side - Electroclinical seizure: nil. - Nonepileptiform features: Frequent asynchronous delta waves in bilateral frontotemporal regions. - Artifacts: eye movements or muscle activity, <50% of the tracing involving <50% of the electrodes - Single-channel electrocardiogram: Arrhythmia. ● Intermittent photic stimulation: no augmentation of slowing ● Hyperventilation: omitted. 【Impression】 Abnormal. - Bilateral frontal delta slowing with intermittent sharpish, especially right side. - Moderate slowing of the background activity 【Clinical correlation】 - Diffuse slowing of the background activity reflects a moderate diffuse cortical dysfunction, which can be seen with toxic-metabolic or systemic causes, or neurodegenerative disorders, and also with cortical injury. - The bilateral frontal sharpish suggest focal hypersynchrony in a patient with a clinical diagnosis of epilepsy. Reference: Tatum IV, W. O., Selioutski, O., Ochoa, J. G., Clary, H. M., Cheek, J., Drislane, F. W., & Tsuchida, T. N. (2016). American clinical neurophysiology society guideline 7: guidelines for EEG reporting. The Neurodiagnostic Journal, 56(4), 285-293.
